Was that Isak’s moment? Gakpo rolls the ball back to Isak in a good shooting position just inside the box, but he slices his left-footed effort well over the bar. More cheers from the Newcastle fans.

Newcastle really should have three! Defence-splitting pass from Miley to release Hall, who feeds a teasing cross into the six-yard box, but Wissa could only get studs on it. Better connection and that was a goal. Liverpool so fragile at the back, though.

Stuart Atwell has been guessing on decisions throughout this game, and Jacob Ramsey has just been booked for what looked a clean challenge on Isak, who produced a lovely turn initially. Newcastle survive the free-kick.

But then Gakpo has acres of space to run into, but Botman saves the day in the box. The game is haywire at the moment.

Here come the Liverpool changes: Ngumoha, who was the match-winner last season here, Wirtz are the players off, replaced by Munoz and Mac Allister.

Liverpool will be kicking themselves, they had Newcastle on the ropes. Iraola is preparing a triple sub. Willock was the goalscorer, but it was also a brilliant assist from Wissa.

The equaliser had been coming but that was really poor from a defensive perspective as everyone backed off Cody Gakpo and let him pick his spot.

You also have to question the decision to keep Will Osula on. He was obviously struggling to move freely and it has meant Newcastle did not have an out ball.

But, just as I was going to be critical of manager Matthias Jassile one of his substitutes puts Newcastle back in front and it a brilliant goal. Magnificent build up play from Wissa, who skipped away from three Liverpool players, but it is even better from Joe Willock who takes the pass in his stride, shows great skill t o take it on jis stride and away from Frimpong and the finish is sublime, curled into the bottom corner.

Jaissle can claim that as a magical substitution, but it is superb individual goal from Joe Willock. Another Newcastle counter-attack, Wissa does brilliantly to wriggle away from three players in midfield, and Willock dribbles inside Frimpong before arcing a shot into the far corner. Outstanding finish.

"Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK

Jaissle with a double sub immediately after conceding: Joe Willock and Jacob Ramsey are on, replacing William Osula and Sean Steur who was a little slack on the Gakpo goal.

The game is one-way traffic, Liverpool looking to turn the screw.

The man linked with a move to Spurs all summer has equalised for Liverpool. He had a sighter a few minutes earlier, and it was too easy for Gakpo to receive the ball behind Newcastle’s midfield, and he had time to pick out the far corner with a clean hit from outside the box. Game on.

Cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v

Just two touches inside the Newcastle penalty area from Isak so far, he has been subdued. Nice idea from Gakpo, chopping inside from the left, and curling a shot not far wide of the top corner.

Good defending from Lewis Hall up against Ngumoha, before Van Dijk passes the ball straight of play. Wissa wanted a free-kick for a challenge from behind by Gravenberch but the referee judged he touched the ball first.

Scramble at the back post from the Liverpool corner, but then a loose touch from Wirtz prompts a Newcastle break and there was a chance for Elanga to dribble into the box but he put the breaks on.

The game is already really stretched, holes appearing in Liverpool’s midfield. Wissa’s poked through ball towards Osula was just a tad overhit.

Liverpool have made a sharp start from kick off, winning a corner.

Just because it is a manager’s first game, we shouldn’t pull our punches. That was a scandalous first half performance from Liverpool and there is absolutely no difference in watching them now compared to what they offered through much of last season. Maybe the disappointment wasn’t about the man in the dugout. Maybe it was about the players wearing the Red shirt.

5 & 18 - 5 - Liverpool have conceded in the opening five minutes on MD1 of a Premier League season for the very first time.The Reds are winless in 18 Premier League away games when falling 1-0 behind (D6 L12) since beating Crystal Palace 2-1 in December 2023.Baptism. pic.twitter.com/K1HF2wNRVP

Newcastle will be delighted to go in leading the game at half time but there were some worrying signs before the break.

They had stopped getting up the pitch and were invited a lot of pressure from Liverpool. Will Osula has clearly picked up an injury – he took a whack on his achilles midway through the half – and will surely need to be replaced by Nick Woltemade in the second half with Yoane Wissa moving up top.

Alexander Isak has been on the receiving end of a number of heavy tackles and has looked pretty miserable so far on his return to St James’ Park.

But Liverpool are not going to keep getting into dangerous positions and fail to capitalise on them. Things for Matthias Jaissle to sort out before the second half.

LFC Midfield all bombing forward happened all pre season, madness!

Plenty of possession for Liverpool, but not enough cutting edge of crispness in their play in the final third. On top of that problem, they were vulnerable to Newcastle’s pace and direct play early on although that threat abated as the half progressed. Jaissle will be delighted with the commitment and application of his players, but Osula may have to come off with a knock.

Isak hooks a pass towards Frimpong straight out of play, causing much mirth among the home fans.

Foul given against Wissa on Gravenberch, and the Newcastle forward needs to be careful on a yellow. I’m not sure there was any contact at all. Wissa drags a shot across the face of Liverpool’s goal and wide.

Gravenberch with a speculative shot which is blocked, before Dedic blasts the ball off Gakpo to win a goal kick. Dan Burn is watching on from the stands, Newcastle’s new club captain who is absent because of a rolled ankle. Also up there in the gods is England manager Thomas Tuchel.

Much better cross from Frimpong, but Dedic clears at the back post for a Liverpool corner. Danger as Gakpo flicks the ball on at the neat post, and the ball bounces off Botman and behind for another corner. Gravenberch tries a cute reverse pass towards Isak, but it deflects through to Hornicek. Isak has been ever so quiet.

William Osula is hobbling up top for Newcastle, which is a worry because has been a menace so far. The same can be said of Yoane Wissa who is having a stormer as a second striker, dropping into midfield at times.

Stuart Atwell being a little card happy, now Lewis Miley is shown a yellow for a foul on Gravenberch. Just looked a regulation midfield foul, not sure a booking was necessary.

Osula took the free-kick, straight into the wall, but his follow up effort deflects off Szoboszlai and behind for a corner. Excellent delivery from Lewis Hall, cleared by Van Dijk.

Wirtz and Isak do well down the left to start a Liverpool counter with runners forward, but Frimpong’s delivery from the right is atrocious.

Liverpool starting to monopolise possession, without a crafty final pass. Kerkez has been booked for holding Elanga, who is giving him a going over on Newcastle’s right flank.

Then Barnes rolls inside Frimpong and drives inside, and the Liverpool right-back is booked for a challenge from behind. May well have been a harsh call, both plays were grasping for a piece of shirt.

Both of Liverpool’s full-backs on yellows now.

Wissa booked for a mistimed challenge, and Liverpool have a free-kick 30 yards out. Szoboszlai is thinking about a shot... but he blasts his shot straight into the wall.

Osula then does very well to make it stick and drag Newcastle up the pitch but the move fizzles out.

It’s an experience in itself watching Andoni Iraola on the sideline. You would expect Liverpool to score at some point but this is a team that has lots of questions to answer.

Isak down on the turf after a strong challenge by Lewis Hall, no foul given much to the delight of the Newcastle fans.

Then the home team cut through Liverpool again, Wissa with a glorious outside of the foot pass behind Jacquet for the run of Osula, but the Liverpool defender just about got a toe to the ball as the striker closed in on Alisson. Great challenge in the end from the wrong side.

Nice counter-movement between Elanga and Dedic the right-back. Elanga faked to drop inside, taking Kerkez and Gakpo with him, and Miley’s switch found Dedic on the outside. Cross is blocked, and Newcastle have a corner. Cleared, and then a poor Szoboszlai pass is blocked when there was a chance to release Wirtz on the counter.

It feels like all the 50:50s are dropping Newcastle’s way at the moment. It has been a very energetic start, the question is whether that is sustainable across the game so early in the season. The tempo will surely drop at some point.

Peter Beardsley, Tino Asprilla and Shaka Hislop among Keegan’s former players watching on.

Hornicek with his first big save of the game, tipping Wirtz’s shot around the post. Newcastle failed to deal with a Kerkez cross and the ball dropped to the German for a snap shot. Newcastle defend the corner.

“There’s only one greedy b-----d,” is the chant from the Newcastle fans (aimed at Isak, for the uninitiated).

Wissa goes down looking for a foul but nothing doing, but there are cheers from the home fans as Isak is beaten to a header and then Sean Steur turns away from pressure well in midfield. There is more bite about the home team in the challenges than Liverpool, Jaissle will be delighted with this.

Echoes of last season with Liverpool’s defence looking suspect against direct play, Alisson with an unconvincing intervention outside his penalty area after the ball held up. He is fortunate that Wissa did not connect with the volley when there was a chance to lob the goalkeeper.

What a difference a year makes. Anthony Elanga was played in on goal against Aston Villa on his Premier League debut for Newcastle United 12 months ago. He looked nervous and hit a tame effort too close to the goalkeeper.

It is fair to say that was a sign of things to come for the winger who endured a miserable first season on Tyneside following a high-profile £55m move from Nottingham Forest. He looked drained of confidence and lacked the composure and technical ability to succeed in black and white stripes.

Fast forward 12 months and he has just taken a very similar chance against Liverpool. The speed of Will Osula sent the visiting defence into retreat, and his pace and excellent first touch set up the chance, which he finished clinically.

That was the player Eddie Howe thought he was signing last summer. It was the player Newcastle supporters thought was going to offer a major upgrade in the right wing position.

If Elanga has a better season this time around it will be a huge boost to new manager Matthias Jaissle.

Elanga vs Kerkez is a match-up which looks advantageous for Newcastle, the Liverpool left-back is at full tilt to get back and by a foul after a lofted Wissa pass over his head towards the rapid Sweden winger.

This is a very open game already, and Liverpool are back on the front foot. Szoboszlai whips in a free-kick which appears to glance of Van Dijk’s head, but the referee awards a corner. Hall clears, but Newcastle do not clear their lines and Gakpo’s shot is blocked by Thiaw.

Liverpool caught out on the break, but it is a really well-executed goal from Newcastle’s perspective. Gravenberch should have let fly at the other end, but after the move broke down Osula was able to receive in space and turn to face Van Dijk and Jacquet. He waited for the support of Elanga to arrive, and he burned down the outside of Kerkez. Well-weighted pass put him through, and the finish across Alisson was ideal.

An electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F

Lewis Hall wins a challenge at the edge of the box which receives a roar of approval from the crowd, but Liverpool quickly settle into a long spell of possession, with Gravenberch turning away from pressure, but neglecting to shoot.

This already has the feel of a very helter-skelter game. Newcastle won a free-kick inside 20 seconds, clipped into the penalty area but it was claimed by Alisson. Then a Liverpool attack swept from one end to the other with Wirtz’s shot blocked at the edge of the box. This should be tasty.

That roar turns to vociferous boos as Alexander Isak takes the kick-off.

They would have still been clapping until tomorrow if the whistle hadn’t been blown by referee Stuart Attwell to start the game but the flip from adulation for Kevin Keegan to absolute vitriol towards Alexander Isak was incredible. 50,000 in black and white are singing a song aimed at him. The only two words we can get away with printing are “ole, ole!” - use your imagination for what might have preceded it!

A period of applause for Kevin Keegan at St James' Park 👏❤️ pic.twitter.com/AsSGOkpVPN

There is a minute’s applause for Keegan, which ends with a defending roar.

Liverpool have just taken to the field for their warm up, predictably to a back drop of pantomime booing. But there is a nice touch from the club, as each member of Andoni Iraola’s squad is wearing a jersey with “Keegan 7” on the back. It’s going to be a day of heavy emotion.

Alan Shearer was one of those fans holding up a white card:

The Keegan quote on the Newcastle banner is: “I want people to dream about their football club. They should, we should all be dreamers at heart. Some people are the opposite and say ‘we can’t do that’, but when you ask them why, they can’t give a reason. Well, I say, ‘Why not?’”

Banners are being unfurled in the Gallowgate End. Alan Shearer and Stuart Pearce are in the stands, and Les Ferdinand is pitchside speaking on Sky.

As you know it’s a transition phase and a huge challenge. There will be some activity in the transfer market new week, hopefully, but we go for it, we are as ready as we can be. That’s something we want to show the fans, we want to go all in.

As soon as I saw him on the pitch, I was falling in love. He is a great guy with great potential.

I’m not worried. As a manager, a player or a squad, if it is against you you want to play this kind of games.

Difficult call, Jeremy has very good skills with the ball, without the ball they will be very demanding today, playing against Wissa and Osula.

Alexander Isak is going to be in for the sort of hostile afternoon unseen in English football for years.

Not since Michael Owen has a player left Newcastle and been so universally despised. Owen was accused of ducking out of a relegation battle to ensure he secured a lucrative free transfer move after an injury-ravaged spell in the North East.

If anything, Isak was even worse, He went on strike, refusing to play for the club again, despite having three years left on his contract, in order to force a move to Liverpool. It felt like the ultimate betrayal and crossed a line with Geordies. They will love you and worship players as good as Isak, but if you behave like the Sweden international did you become the ultimate villain.

Isak was a superb player in black and white stripes, arguably their best since the takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund in 2021. He was top goalscorer two years running and was the focal point of Eddie Hower’s attack as they qualified for the Champions League twice and won the Carabao Cup.

He could have been a Geordie legend, but he left in such an ugly and acrimonious fashion. Isak forced Newcastle to buckle from their not for sale stance, rejecting a pay rise and a new contract, insisting he would never play for the club again even if they refused to sell him, that he will be tarnished forever.

It is sad in many ways and shows the ugly side of the game. I’m told he does regret the manner of his exit, especially his falling out with Howe. They have not spoken since. It has weighed heavily on him since his move to Anfield.

Looks like Rio Ngumoha will play on the right flank with Cody Gakpo left, Wirtz in the No 10 role behind Isak.

Liverpool XI: Alisson; Frimpong, Van Dijk, Jacquet, Kerkez; Gravenberch, Szoboszlai; Ngumoha, Wirtz, Gakpo; Isak

The Reds to take on Newcastle in our season opener ✊ #NEWLIV

Barnes, Wissa, Osula and Elanga start in what could be a front four. Lewis Miley and Sean Steur, just 20 and 18 respectively, will need to get through an immense amount of work in midfield.

Newcastle United XI: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw (c), Botman, Hall; Miley, Steur; Elanga, Wissa, Barnes; Osula

Sir Kenny Dalglish and Bobby Moncur are the representatives of both clubs with wreaths, and Shola Ameobi is behind Dalglish. Ian Rush is also in attendance, who spent one season on Tyneside in the twilight of his career when Dalglish was the manager.

There will be a powerful expression of unity between Newcastle United and Liverpool supporters in memory of their shared icon, Kevin Keegan, before this afternoon’s game.

A man who meant so much to both clubs: a phenomenal player for Liverpool and a force of nature who transformed Newcastle as both a player and a manager.

The cooperation between the two to ensure St James’ Park can deliver a special tribute to a remarkable figure in English football has been heartwarming.

The sale of Curtis Jones to Inter Milan means that for the first time since Liverpool came into existence in 1892, the prospect of them going through the season without fielding a player who was born in the city for a game is real. That will surely sting Liverpool fans more than most, given the city’s strong sense of regional identity. You can read more on the subject in this article by Dominic King. Trent on loan in January, anyone?

He has also not sugar-coated anything. Jaissle knows he is up against it. Time is the enemy, given how late he arrived in pre-season and he understands the size of the task ahead.

These are early days, but the energy and purpose he has brought to the job have impressed everyone at all levels of the club. Clear communication is at the heart of everything. He explains what he expects, what he needs and what has to be done, no matter who the conversation is with.

It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.Full team news on the way shortly.

#1830. Jesus de Miguel: Tenerife player dies in hospital one day after goalkeeper collision

CD Tenerife player Jesus De Miguel has died following an on-field collision during a match on Monday, the club has confirmed.

The incident occurred during stoppage time of a Spanish second-tier fixture as Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono rushed from his goal to challenge De Miguel for the ball.

In a statement on Tuesday, the Canary Islands club said: "Racked with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic passing, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8::green-background[00] a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda.

"There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness.

Late on Monday, Tenerife initially confirmed De Miguel had been hospitalised and was "stable despite the severity of his condition". However, an update early on Tuesday morning stated his condition had "worsened neurologically".

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style

Owono was shown a red card after charging into the centre circle, where his knee appeared to connect with De Miguel’s head. Players from both sides immediately signalled for medical help and were visibly distressed before the match was suspended.

Andorra issued a statement on X reading: "With broken hearts and devastated, we want to send our most sincere condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, to all his teammates, friends, and to CD Tenerife. Rest in peace."

LaLiga said: "We wish to express our deep sadness over the tragic passing of Jesús de Miguel Alameda. We share in the grief of his family, his loved ones, and @CDTOficial during these very difficult times. All our affection and support. Rest in peace."

Every football match scheduled in Spain for Tuesday has been postponed by the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF), including Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina ties.

The governing body also cancelled the official presentation for Spain’s Under-21 match against Japan out of respect and solidarity with De Miguel’s family, team-mates and Tenerife supporters.

UEFA announced that a period of silence will be observed before all European games this week, with Spanish sides Atletico Madrid, Barcelona and Villarreal competing in the Champions League.

"We are heartbroken by the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin said. "We have searched for words and found only silence."

Other Spanish clubs also expressed their condolences. Barcelona said: "From FC Barcelona, we are deeply saddened by the tragic news of the passing of Jesus de Miguel, CD Tenerife player. Our thoughts and support are with his family, friends and loved ones during these difficult times."

Real Madrid said the club "wishes to express its condolences and affection to his family, his teammates, his club and all his loved ones".

#1829. Arsenal transfer news: Gunners, Spurs, Bayern Munich 'suffer blow' in pursuit of Premier League midfielder

By Darren Plant | 02 Nov 2026 15:49

Arsenal are one of a number of clubs to allegedly suffer a blow in their efforts to sign Nottingham Forest midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White.

The Gunners moved to the top of the Premier League table on Sunday with an impressive 1-0 victory at Liverpool.

Sitting three points clear of Manchester City, there is an argument that Mikel Arteta does not need to add to his first-team squad.

However, Arsenal sometimes lack quality in the final third and could benefit from a player of Gibbs-White's profile.

As per Football Insider, Arsenal and other interested parties may struggle to get a deal over the line for the England international.

The report alleges that Forest have no interest in entertaining any offers for the 26-year-old at the midway point of the campaign.

That is despite the playmaker's contract being due to expire in 2028. At this point in time, he is unlikely to consider a renewal.

Under Oliver Glasner, Forest have accumulated just six points from their opening nine Premier League matches of 2026-27.

Forest are seemingly prioritising having Gibbs-White in their team to try to guide them up the standings, rather than looking to cash in on his services for the highest fee possible.

Tottenham Hotspur and Bayern Munich are also said to be admirers of Gibbs-White.

With 37 goals and 37 assists from 179 appearances in all competitions, Gibbs-White is already cemented as a Forest legend.

However, it feels inevitable that he will eventually want to move to a bigger club to play in the Champions League and more regularly for England.

Although Forest can play hardball over a fee to a certain extent, they can ill-afford to risk losing their most prized asset on a free transfer in 2028.

Gibbs-White will know this and likely stay patient until the end of this season.

#1828. Jesse Derry back at Chelsea tonight in Sporting loan twist

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Champions League football at Stamford Bridge awaits Jesse Derry this evening.

The Chelsea youngster is on loan at Sporting in Portugal this season, but is back to the Blues’ home ground in west London to face off against Shakhtar Donetsk, who are calling the Bridge their home in Europe's premier competition this season due to the ongoing conflict in the Donbas region.

Derry will be hoping to be given the chance to make an impact, with some Chelsea fans no doubt watching on among those who head to Stamford Bridge for an evening of Champions League entertainment.

It will be the first time Derry has appeared at Chelsea’s home ground since his Premier League debut in May, when he was taken to hospital midway through the game after a sickening clash of heads with Nottingham Forest’s Zach Abbott from which he has now recovered.

Derry has had to be patient so far for opportunities to show Sporting why they opted to take him on loan for the season but may have turned a corner last week.

After all of his first six appearances for the club came in the form of cameos as a substitute, he was finally handed his first start for the Lisbon giants when they faced Maritimo in the Portuguese League Cup. Derry chipped in with his first goal involvement for the club, assisting the opening goal as Sporting prevailed 2-1 on the night.

The chance is there for Derry to make his first Champions League start this evening if interim head coach Tiago Fernandes calls on him.

The 19-year-old will be hoping his 73 minutes in the tank last week can pave the way for further minutes this evening, especially after struggling to play as much as he’d have liked so far. #1826. Arsenal pay touching tribute to Jesus de Miguel after tragic death

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal paid tribute to Jesus de Miguel after the 30-year-old died from injuries suffered in a Spanish second-division match.

The Tenerife striker had serious injuries to his head and chest after colliding with goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a game against FC Andorra on Monday.

Owono's knee collided heavily with De Miguel, who was treated on the pitch for more than five minutes before being taken by ambulance to hospital.

His condition was said to be "stable despite the severity of his condition" on Monday, however that deteriorated and De Miguel died on Tuesday morning.

Tributes have been paid to De Miguel across the game, including from Kylian Mbappe and Gerard Pique, who co-owns Andorra.

Arsenal responded to the tragic news themselves as players and staff gathered at the start of their training session on Tuesday morning.

The Gunners huddled in a circle and observed a period of silence in front of a big screen with a picture of De Miguel on.

The Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) has postponed all matches scheduled for Tuesday.

UEFA announced that a period of silence take place before every European games this week, which will include matches involving Spanish sides Atletico Madrid, Barcelona and Villarreal.

"We are heartbroken by the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin ‌said. "We have searched for words and found only silence."

In a statement announcing De Miguel's death, Tenerife said: "Racked with pain, with ‌a lump in our throats and unable to ​believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic ​passing of Jesus de ⁠Miguel Alameda.

"There are no words of comfort; there is ‌absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness."

#1825. Lisandro Martinez's self-destruction sums up a broken Man United as Michael Carrick's future hangs by a thread - and there are still questions to ask of Xabi Alonso's Chelsea, writes IAN HERBERT

By IAN HERBERT, DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 10:52 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 12:01 EDT, 31 October 2026

The sun was high and fierce and Michael Carrick shielded his eyes from it on the few occasions he got to his feet and tried to direct the Manchester United players, who did not seem to hear him. The United contingent hurled personal abuse at Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Jason Wilcox. The scrutiny was remorseless and unyielding.

For a time, there seemed to be hope - and no one can say that this latest hammer blow for Carrick removes the doubts about Xabi Alonso’s methods – but it was crushed by the same fecklessness and mindlessness that is burying United alive.

Carrick did not cast so much as a glance at Lisandro Martinez - who had just finished off the team’s hopes by leaping with Wesley Fofana and extending an elbow into his face to concede a penalty - when he walked past on the way to the tunnel.

Bruno Fernandes and some others made a half-hearted protest about the dismissal but Carrick didn’t. He knew. This looked for all the world like a footballer looking to leave the field early – making no attempt to play the ball as he was up with Fofana, having been booked for a reckless challenge on Morgan Rogers, just three minutes earlier.

The Argentinian, whose words publicly challenging the club a few weeks back will always belong to the story of these Carrick-era death throes, will perhaps want to trash talk the club again when he has been shown the door. But it was also his own gross inadequacy which had allowed Morgan Rogers to dance through the defence to put Chelsea ahead. Martinez should never darken the door of a United squad again.

Michael Carrick’s future at Manchester United looks increasingly untenable after his side imploded in the second half to lose 2-0 against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge

Lisandro Martinez, publicly outspoken earlier this month, was booked twice inside two minutes

There are few grounds for optimism from here but Fernandes is one. When he forfeited the chance to write a new script for himself – blasting into the stand after Bryan Mbeumo’s cross had gifted him a golden opportunity – the prospect of him righting the wrongs of the past week seemed forlorn.

By then, he had already been dumped on his backside by Romeo Lavia and Moises Caicedo and ceded possession. But he brushed off the mockery of the Chelsea faithful to put in a performance which demonstrated that he has a part to play at United.

In front of the small United away section before the game, he went through a free-kick taking routine, arcing one into the top-left corner and striking another against the bar.

He was the one who saw the picture late in the first half, sliding in a pass which sent Amad in. When United went 2-0 down, he conferred with Carrick. He lingered before United’s fans at the end and they accepted him. The turmoil remains but he will be needed.

Fernandes was the one who saw the picture late in the first half, sliding in a pass which sent Amad in and United went 2-0 down, he conferred with Carrick

There can be no overstating the gravity of the week just passed for Xabi Alonso: a lamentable performance in defeat to Tottenham, the Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool and the Spaniard’s suggestion that trophy didn’t matter, which has gone down badly with the fans.

His brief programme notes made it clear how much he wanted something better here but the yawning gaps between Chelsea’s midfield and defensive lines and the ease with which United exploited them in the first half were disturbing. Wesley Fofana was lamentable.

United’s Amad could have plundered them twice – first burgling Fofana on the half-way line but lacking the pace to accelerate on and score, then easing into space and failing to despatch when one-on-one with Mike Penders. Cole Palmer’s error allowed Matheus Cunha to send Fernandes off but Mbeumo couldn’t connect with his cross. United’s failure to capitalise was fateful.

Wesley Fofana was lamentable and United’s Amad Diallo could have plundered them twice

As both sides squandered chances and laboured under basic defensive challenges, it was hard to countenance the notion that two gladiators of European football used to compete in this fixture and actually contested a Champions League final.

The occasion cried out for a moment of class and it was Morgan Rogers who provided it, taking a ball Romeo Lavia had won, dancing his way through half of the Manchester United team and slipping the ball home.

The defending shamed the traditions of the visiting team. Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos, Martinez and Harry Maguire just watched Morgan go. But it was Rogers, taking his Chelsea tally to six goals and four assists in all competitions, who turned the game around.

Morgan Rogers had scored a brilliant solo goal for Chelsea's second-half opener to show up United’s awful finishing

It was always clear that the test of United’s mettle would come if they fell behind. The general view of the fans marching through Euston Station at 11am was that if United scored first they would come away with the points. If they conceded, their heads would drop and the psychological failure at the heart of this team would come to the fore. And so it came to pass.

In a straw poll of 15 or so at Euston, only two thought Carrick was the man to restore ‘Standards’, to quote the mantra captured on an Old Trafford banner last week. The way Chelsea turned the screw just bore that pessimism. Cole Palmer converted the penalty Martinez had conceded to finish things off.

It was to the jubilant cheers of the Chelsea faithful that Estevao left the field towards the end and this was an afternoon which will live long in the memory for him. Twice he had the ball in United’s net – pouncing on Senne Lammens' failure to hold a cross in the first half and taking Palmer’s pass to crash home in the second – but twice he was denied by VAR.

By the end, he had the control of Chelsea’s right as he interlinked with Palmer and came close a third time. Some will say this calls into question Alonso’s decision to limit his game time so far, though it was only as United fell away to nothing that he ran the show.

Some will say Estevao's display calls into question Alonso’s decision to limit his game time so far, though it was only as United fell away to nothing that he ran the show

As the minutes ticked down on another desperate result for United, the away section sang Carrick’s name once more and, significantly, he walked over towards them alone once more, just as he had after the defeat at home to Bournemouth. But it was a less emphatic assertion of empathy and support for him this time, and he did not linger so long.

The talk of Eddie Howe’s availability grows. It emerged on Saturday that under the terms of his departure agreement with Newcastle United that he will cost United only £3million. The United fans are really not convinced by him and it looks like the club will work through many more managers before a corner is turned. The constant will be that support base, who began and ended the match singing Sir Matt Busby’s name. They will always have their history.

#1824. What Chelsea must do to sign Alex Scott after Bournemouth owner's transfer update

By Ben Knapton | 02 Nov 2026 16:08

Chelsea must not make a move for Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott before deciding on the futures of their own engine-room enforcers, a Blues legend has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Chelsea are believed to have identified Scott as their leading January transfer target, after trying and failing to lure the England international away from the Vitality Stadium during the summer transfer window.

Chelsea are supposedly 'completely focused' on signing Scott over the winter, although Liverpool, Manchester City and Manchester United have not yet given up hope of winning the race either.

Bournemouth owner Bill Foley recently delivered an update on Scott's future, insisting that the Cherries have not given up hope of tying him to a new deal beyond 2028, but admitting that young players can sometimes get "stars in their eyes".

Asked by Sports Mole whether Scott could fill Enzo Fernandez's boots at Chelsea, Gus Poyet gave the transfer his seal of approval but implored his former club to sort out which of their midfielders can be moved on first.

"I like the player," Poyet said. "I have seem him a lot and I think he is a very good player. Chelsea need to first decide on the players at the club first, before looking to sign anyone else.

"They have to decide what the future is as they have Caicedo, Lavia, James and others in the centre of midfield, so they must identify who will be the main starters and then move forward on whether Scott is the player they want and then who will then move on."

Scott previously spent one season in the Bournemouth academy between 2016 and 2017, before making a name for himself at Bristol City and earning a return to the Cherries in 2023 for £19.2m.

The midfielder has since scored seven goals and set up seven more for Bournemouth across all tournaments, while winning his first two senior England caps during the September/October international break.

However, it was on Scott's first start for England against Croatia that he aggravated his hamstring injury, and it remains to be seen if he is selected for Thomas Tuchel's November squad.

Chelsea currently have five recognised central midfielders on the books in Moises Caicedo, Valentin Barco, Jordan Henderson, Romeo Lavia and Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli, while Reece James and Malo Gusto can fill in if required.

The fledgling Nicoll-Jazuli is only 16 years of age, though, and will likely spend another two or three years either developing with the youth team or out on loan regardless of whether Chelsea sign Scott.

Henderson - 20 years Nicoll-Jazuli's senior - is only under contract until 2028, at which point he will be 38 years old, and it is difficult to envisage the Englishman sticking around for longer than 24 months.

Meanwhile, Barco and Caicedo's contracts run to 2033, while the injury-plagued Lavia is tied down to 2030 and has shown signs of a revival alongside Caicedo in recent weeks.

If Scott were to arrive in January, the 23-year-old should immediately battle Lavia to partner Caicedo in Xabi Alonso's engine room, with Barco and Henderson providing youthful and experienced backup options.

Gus Poyet was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of William Hill sports betting.

#1823. Surprise! Mikel Arteta reunited with former Arsenal striker before Champions League clash

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Yaya Sanogo paid a surprise visit to Arsenal ahead of their Champions League fixture against Slavia Prague.

The Frenchman, who was a team-mate of Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta from 2013 to 2016, was spotted at London Colney on Tuesday morning as the squad were put through their paces during training.

It is not clear as to why Sanogo was present at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, but he was able to catch up with Arteta prior to the Spaniard going to oversee preparations for the Champions League clash.

The session in question also saw the return of Sanogo’s compatriot William Saliba as he stepped up his rehabilitation from a back injury that sidelined him since the World Cup semi-final in July.

Sanogo spent four years at Arsenal upon joining from Auxerre on a free transfer as he caught Arsene Wenger’s eye, at the time, after scoring seven goals in the same week.

“For all the problems I’d had, the phone wouldn’t ring for two years," Sanogo recalled when speaking to Masterclass media. "But after my seven goals in two games, Arsene Wenger calls me.

“I had a little Motorola, I promise you I had that phone. I was at home using my Macbook and I saw +44. I’m thinking ‘What is this number?’ So I don’t answer, but he called again.

“I say ‘Hello’. ‘Hello, it’s Arsene Wenger’. I thought it was a joke.

“I say ‘Yes?’ ‘It’s Yaya Sanogo?’ I say ‘Yes’. And I don’t speak.

“He tells me ‘Everybody is talking about you, seven goals in one week, not many players have done it’. And I told him ‘Yes, thank you, that’s nice’. But I didn’t know what to say.

“He told me ‘I see you are shy. I’m getting my plane and I want to meet you. I don’t know if you care, I know there’s a lot of clubs that want you, especially after the week you had. Would you be interested to meet me in Paris?’

“I said ‘Yes’ but I don’t realise. I think it’s amazing. He asked me when it’s OK to come to Paris and he hung up.

“I’m saying ‘Wait, wait, it was really Wenger?’ I had two years of problems. Six, seven games [later], Wenger calls me. I’ll sign right now.”

Ultimately, Sanogo was not able to forge a successful career at Arsenal as his only goal for the club came in a 2-0 Champions League group stage win over Borussia Dortmund in November 2014.

#1820. Why West Ham fans should welcome - and be wary of - Scott Parker appointment

Scott Parker is the frontrunner to succeed Nuno Espirito Santo, who was sacked as West Ham head coach on Tuesday morning with the club’s promotion hopes hanging in the balance.

West Ham were widely considered favourites to bounce straight back to the Premier League this season, but after six wins from their first 13 Championship games, they are down in eighth place.

Having recorded a £104.2million loss in the last financial year, the club are acutely aware of the financial imperative of returning to the top flight at the first opportunity and have moved swiftly to make a change in the dugout following successive home defeats to Southampton and West Brom.

Parker, a club legend who won three successive Player of the Year awards during a four-year stint in east London, is seen as someone who can not only get supporters back onside but has experience getting teams promoted from the Championship.

The 46-year-old has earned promotion to the Premier League on three separate occasions across spells with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley, but his success has not come without criticism.

His time at Fulham, who offered him his first senior managerial role in May 2019, was dominated by tensions with the board, and Parker openly criticised the club’s long-term structure and recruitment.

West Ham agree new manager appointment after Nuno sacking

West Ham confirm Nuno Espirito Santo sack decision as statement issued

Nuno under pressure as West Ham sent tumbling down Championship table

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

Despite taking Fulham up from the Championship, Parker then struggled to build a competitive Premier League side and presided over a dispiriting relegation campaign, with his pragmatic style of play proving increasingly unpopular with supporters.

Parker left Fulham by mutual consent after their relegation in 2021 before swiftly taking charge at Bournemouth. While not direct rivals, the move left a bitter taste for some, with Bournemouth in direct competition with Fulham for promotion from the Championship.

Both teams went up automatically during the 2021/22 season. But while Fulham were able to stabilise under the guidance of Marco Silva, similar issues reared their head for Parker, and he was sacked four games into the season after questioning the direction and commitment of the club following a 9-0 defeat to Liverpool.

Parker’s comments, in which he said his team were "ill-equipped at this level", led Bournemouth’s then-owner Maxim Demin to hit back, stating that for the club to progress, everyone must “show belief in and respect for one another.”

Scott Parker is a manager with pedigree at this level but also plenty of baggage

West Ham will be aware of Parker’s history, including an ill-fated 67-day spell at Belgian side Club Brugge, and they will have made it clear during negotiations that he must secure promotion to secure his future.

After a toxic end to Nuno’s tenure, there will be a fair amount of goodwill for the former England international given his cult status at the club and his knowledge of the league.

The Championship is relentless, though, and results need to change quickly if West Ham are to keep pace with the top of the table and stop the chasing pack from gaining encouragement.

In Parker, West Ham believe they have a safe pair of hands who knows the club and knows how to get out of the Championship. Supporters are, however, bound to be more sceptical.

Parker’s vision for West Ham will almost certainly be built on defensive solidity, and with good reason. West Ham have conceded 18 goals in 13 league games this season, a rate of 1.4 goals per game.

Given the quality of the squad at his disposal, though, there will also be an expectation to entertain. West Ham, for all their struggles, have at times blown teams away this season, scoring in every game this term.

Parker is a manager with pedigree at this level but also plenty of baggage. West Ham can’t say they have not been warned.

#1819. Borussia Dortmund vs Real Betis - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 16:17, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 14:15

BVB Stadion will play host to an intriguing Champions League fixture on Wednesday evening, as Borussia Dortmund welcome Real Betis.

Dortmund are 13th in the Champions League league stage table, picking up six points from three matches, while Betis are fifth in the rankings on nine points.

Dortmund opened their 2026-27 Champions League league stage campaign with a 3-2 home success over Villarreal, before suffering a 1-0 defeat to Bodo/Glimt in their second match, but they returned to winning ways last time out, beating Sabah 2-1.

A return of six points from three matches has left BVB in 13th spot in the overall table, and they will bring a five-game unbeaten run into this contest, including a 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga on Saturday night.

Dortmund, who have won three of their last four matches during a strong run, are preparing to face Real Betis for the first time, but they have won each of their last four UEFA matches against Spanish opposition, all of which have been at home.

Niko Kovac's side will follow this match with back-to-back Bundesliga games against Elversberg and Borussia Monchengladbach, before returning to European action against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium on November 24.

Dortmund reached the Champions League knockout phase playoffs in 2025-26, losing to Atalanta BC, so there is plenty of room for improvement this term.

Real Betis, meanwhile, will enter the match off the back of a 2-1 win over Malaga in La Liga, with the result leaving them fourth in their domestic table.

It has been a strong start to the 2026-27 campaign for Manuel Pellegrini's side, who have been victorious in their opening three matches of this season's Champions League.

The Seville outfit started their European campaign with a 3-2 victory over Lille, before posting a 3-2 win over Porto; six points then became nine courtesy of a 1-0 success over Feyenoord, and they are up in fifth spot in the overall table.

Real Betis reached the quarter-finals of the 2025-26 Europa League, losing to Braga, while they were in the final of the 2024-25 Conference League, being beaten by Chelsea.

El Glorioso last competed in the Champions League in 2005-06, being knocked out in the group stage, but they look capable of advancing to the knockout round of this season's European Cup.

Borussia Dortmund form (all competitions):

Dortmund will be without the services of Kaua Prates (muscle), but the home side are otherwise in strong form for their clash with Real Betis.

Serhou Guirassy has been in strong form this season, scoring eight times and registering two assists in 13 appearances, and the 30-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

Fabio Silva has five goals and two assists in 13 matches this season and will also start, while Jobe Bellingham is in line to feature as an advanced midfielder for the German club.

As for Real Betis, Cucho Hernandez (calf) and Junior Firpo (muscular) are both out of the match, but no fresh issues have been reported.

Three players have scored four times for Real Betis this season - Isco, Marc Bartra and Abde Ezzalzouli - and the trio are set to feature in the first XI.

Troy Parrott has two goals in 11 appearances for the Seville outfit during the 2026-27 campaign and should also feature in the starting side due to Hernandez's absence.

Meanwhile, Antony and Pablo Fornals are expected to be in the XI.

Borussia Dortmund possible starting lineup:

Kobel; Gadou, Anton, Schlotterbeck; Ryerson, Veerman, Nmecha, Svensson; Bellingham; F Silva, Guirassy

Valles; Bellerin, Bartra, Natan, F Garcia; Fornals, Roca; Antony, Isco, Ezzalzouli; Parrott

Real Betis have been excellent in this season's Champions League, and the La Liga club deserve a lot of respect, but Dortmund at home are a tough proposition, and we are backing BVB to edge a close game on Wednesday.

The Frenchman has not played a single minute since he limped off after half an hour of France's World Cup semi-final against Spain.

Saliba was sent to see specialists on that back injury and while it was decided that surgery was not necessary, an extended period of rest has been required.

His recovery has gone well and Saliba has been back on the grass in recent weeks, going through individual training drills.

That has now been stepped up significantly, with Saliba understood to have to been back in first-team training on Monday.

The 25-year-old came through that without any issues and he was involved again on Tuesday morning, as the Arsenal squad trained in front of the media.

Mikel Arteta and his players will fly out to Prague later in the day ahead of facing Slavia Prague on Wednesday night.

It remains to be seen whether Saliba is included in that travelling squad, with Arsenal understandably cautious over his return to action.

The Gunners face Hull on Saturday before then having two weeks off for the November international break, allowing Saliba further time on the training pitch to build his fitness.

Saliba's return will leave Arteta with a serious selection headache heading into another hectic period.

Ezri Konsa, signed in the summer to cover for Saliba's absence, has been superb alongside Gabriel and probably Arsenal's best player so far this season.

The England international's strong form will allow Arsenal to ease Saliba back into action without taking significant risks with his fitness.

#1817. Man United news: Erik ten Hag says relegation "is possible" amid Michael Carrick struggles

By Darren Plant | 02 Nov 2026 16:20

Erik ten Hag has claimed that former club Manchester United cannot rely on reputation alone to avoid relegation from the Premier League.

Man United are currently preparing to face Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday night having not won a game in any competition since September 10.

Although Michael Carrick was defiant in a press conference on Monday, the Red Devils only sit outside of the Premier League relegation zone on goal difference.

Given the players that they have at their disposal and the increasing possibility of appointing a more experienced replacement for Carrick, the assumption is that Man United will retain their top-flight status.

Nevertheless, speaking to ESPN NL's 'Goedemorgen Eredivisie', Ten Hag says that no-one associated with Man United can afford any complacency.

The Dutchman claims that Man United are at risk of being involved in a "vicious circle".

He said: "In the Premier League it's certainly possible, because all the teams are simply strong.

"They're all strong squads, all good managers. And if you end up on the wrong side once and you really get into that vicious circle, then it can become very difficult."

Man United have not suffered relegation from the top flight of English football since 1974.

Of 12 managers who have been in the Man United dugout since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement, only three have lifted silverware.

With a Europa League, League Cup and Community Shield to his name and a win ratio of more than 58% over 144 matches, the stats say that Jose Mourinho is Man United's best manager since Ferguson.

While Ten Hag never had the same affinity with the fans as the Portuguese, he guided the club to a League Cup and FA Cup across a 128-game stint.

Despite his reputation having lowered from his time at Old Trafford, Ten Hag deserves more respect for the job that he did at the Theatre of Dreams.

#1816. Where to watch Manchester United vs Roma: TV channel and live stream for Champions League today

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Manchester United host Roma in the Champions League tonight as Michael Carrick desperately seeks an end to their woeful winless run.

The beleaguered Man Utd boss may now have only two games left to save his job, with a further review expected during the November international break, following Sunday’s home clash with Aston Villa in the Premier League.

Though his side delivered a much-improved first-half display against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, the wheels then swiftly fell off in familiarly chaotic fashion as Lisandro Martinez was dismissed in a 2-0 loss - United’s third in a row and fourth in the last five matches.

They have gone nine matches without a victory for the first time since the 1988/89 season to spark genuine concern over a potential relegation battle, having not won at all since their last Champions League home fixture - the 4-0 drubbing of Azerbaijani debutants Sabah FK on September 10.

But, having lost away at Atletico Madrid and Como since then to slip to 21st in the league phase table, they can expect a much sterner challenge from Roma, who continue to thrive despite a lengthy injury list that has seen them travel to Old Trafford with only 17 available outfield players.

The Giallorossi are in strong form under Gian Piero Gasperini and sit third in Serie A, still unbeaten and four points adrift of leaders Inter Milan after 10 games having won four of their last five matches across all competitions including Saturday’s 5-2 demolition of struggling Udinese.

Roma brushed aside Slovan Bratislava 4-0 in their last Champions League outing, having also been edged out by Real Madrid in a seven-goal thriller and drawn with Fenerbahce to sit 15th.

Carrick will hope to invoke the spirit of 2007, when he scored twice for United in a memorable 7-1 home trouncing of Roma in the Champions League quarter-finals.

TV channel and live stream: Unlike most Champions League fixtures, tonight’s game is not being shown live in the UK on TNT Sports.

Instead, it will be broadcast by Amazon Prime Video, who still have the first pick of one Tuesday night match up until the semi-finals.

Coverage begins at 6:30pm GMT ahead of an 8pm kick-off at Old Trafford, presented by Gabby Logan and featuring punditry from former Man United trio Wayne Rooney, Nicky Butt and Ashley Young.

#1815. Michael Carrick insists he will NOT be sacked as Man United manager - despite side slipping closer to relegation zone after Chelsea defeat

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER

Published: 12:33 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 12:50 EDT, 31 October 2026

Michael Carrick believes he will cling onto his job as Manchester United head coach despite watching helplessly as his team slid closer towards the relegation zone at Chelsea.

Goals from Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer – who converted a penalty after Lisandro Martinez was sent off for picking up two yellow cards in the space of 82 seconds – consigned United to a 2-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge as they sank to 17th(check) place in the Premier League.

Earlier this week, Carrick was given more time by Old Trafford bosses to turn the club’s disastrous season around, but he is now without a win in nine games.

Asked if he will be in charge for Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Roma, he replied: ‘Yes. I'm just looking forward to getting the boys ready for the midweek now.’

The 20-time champions of England are faced with the humiliation of dropping into the bottom three and it was put to Carrick, a player and coach at United stretching back two decades, that seeing the club in such a position must be hurting him.

‘Yeah, pretty much exactly that,’ he said. ‘There is a lot of emotion. We're a great football club and we want to win football matches. Things have gone against us in a big way and unravelled quickly.

Man United are now without a win in nine games in all competitions, their longest such run since October-November 1988

‘There is no hiding from the fact that we haven't won enough games. There's no words that I'm going to explain to you now that makes it any different, it's not going to change it.

‘You can look at how far you can move up the league quite quickly if you win football matches. So that's the way it's got to be approached, for sure.’

Carrick insisted that he didn’t feel let down by Martinez, but did not even look at the Argentine as he left the pitch.

‘It has a major importance on the game. A huge moment. I think that is pretty obvious really,’ added Carrick. ‘The second goal and losing the man at that stage had a big influence on it, for sure.’

The United fans continued to give Carrick their support while once again turning on the club’s owners, the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and director of football Jason Wilcox.

Meanwhile, Xabi Alonso admitted Estevao’s positive performance will give him a selection headache after the wonderkid showed Chelsea what they have been missing.

Morgan Rogers' brilliant solo goal set Chelsea on their way to victory

The 19-year-old Brazilian was handed his first Premier League start of the season and scored two disallowed goals for offside as well as creating several other opportunities.

‘He’s given me reasons (to pick him),’ said Alonso. ‘This is football and sometimes you don’t get what you want, but the best way to show it is not by being angry, it’s by being competitive and Este has done it really well.’

Alonso also hailed Romeo Lavia after the 22-year-old Belgian filled in for the unwell Jordan Henderson in midfield on short notice, and was arguably this game’s best performer.

‘From a midfielder point of view, for me it has been a top, top performance,’ Alonso said. ‘He's done so many things right. He’s been always connecting the defence with the attacker players, he's been able to switch the game, he's taken many right decisions, he's been very dynamic, competitive. I'm very happy for him and he deserves a huge recognition for his performance.’

#1813. Crystal Palace make decision over Jean-Philippe Mateta red card appeal before Liverpool

Crystal Palace have lodged an appeal against the red card awarded to Jean-Philippe Mateta during their 2-0 defeat to Tottenham last Saturday.

Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute, following a VAR review, for a studs-up challenge on Micky van de Ven as the pair contested for a loose ball at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Referee Michael Oliver originally awarded Mateta a yellow card but upgraded his decision after being sent to the monitor to have a second look at the challenge.

With Palace down to 10 men, Spurs took control of the game and sealed a comfortable victory after goals in either half from Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke.

Mateta landed on top of Van de Ven’s right ankle with his studs up as he chased a pass into space, and Oliver deemed the 29-year-old to have used “full forceful contact” as he explained his decision inside the stadium.

Palace’s view, though, is that Mateta’s challenge was accidental, and they argue that the French international had his eyes on the ball and did not see Van de Ven coming.

Mateta currently faces a three-match suspension, but Palace hope the decision is either overturned or his ban reduced.

Pierre Sage, who is under increasing pressure to turn things around at Palace, has only recently welcomed Mateta back into the fold after a hamstring injury and will desperately want his star striker back available.

If Mateta’s ban is upheld, he would miss this weekend’s home game against Liverpool, as well as crunch fixtures against newly promoted teams Coventry and Hull.

He will, however, be available for selection when Palace host Hoffenheim and Real Sociedad in the Europa League.

#1812. Liverpool confirm Ryan Gravenberch injury blow as Andoni Iraola names squad for Champions League clash

Liverpool have been dealt a new injury blow as Ryan Gravenberch will miss the Champions League showdown against Fenerbahce.

Gravenberch has cemented himself as a regular in Liverpool’s midfield since the autumn international break, starting five of the seven matches across all competitions.

He did, however, miss the comeback win over Brentford through suspension after being sent off in the defeat to Manchester City and was then dropped for the 1-0 loss to Arsenal at the weekend.

Gravenberch was expected to be in contention for Liverpool against Fenerbahce on Wednesday, but it has since been revealed that the Dutchman will not be making the trip to Turkey.

A Liverpool statement reads: “A heel injury means the midfielder will not be part of the Reds’ travelling squad for Wednesday’s meeting with the Turkish side in Istanbul.

“He will instead remain at the AXA Training Centre to undergo treatment with the club’s medical team.”

As such, Gravenberch joins Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni and fellow Dutchman Jeremie Frimpong as the five Liverpool injury absentees against Fenerbahce.

Iraola issued an update on the Dutchman on Tuesday: "It is a day to day thing.

“The fracture healed, it is about the pain. He has some discomfort. It is going to be something every day we will ask him how he is."

Wataru Endo and Federico Chiesa, meanwhile, are unavailable due to not being named in the club’s squad list for the Champions League this season.

It remains to be seen if Gravenberch will be fit to face Crystal Palace at the weekend, though he has a battle on his hands to regain a midfield spot from Trey Nyoni.

“The thinking is that he's playing very well and we trust him," Iraola told Sky Sports pre-match of his decision to drop Gravenberch in favour of Nyoni against Arsenal.

#1811. Porto vs Napoli - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 02 Nov 2026 17:13, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 14:16

One of three teams still without a point, Porto will again try to get off the mark in this season's Champions League when Napoli visit Estadio do Dragao on Wednesday evening.

While the Italian side got up and running last time out, they have lost six and won none of their last seven away games at Europe's top level.

Last month's 1-0 home loss to PSV Eindhoven was Porto's third consecutive Champions League defeat, leaving them in danger of failing to make the knockout rounds later this term.

Following previous setbacks against Manchester City and Real Betis, the Dragons have crucially conceded the first goal each time, always putting them on the back foot.

So, approaching the midpoint of this season's league phase, Porto need at least nine points just to reach the playoffs - and that may not even prove enough.

Still facing tough trips to Feyenoord and Liverpool, Francesco Farioli's men must try to maximise home advantage in midweek, having continued their domestic domination last time out.

After ending a three-year wait for the Portuguese title, they have brought that form into the current campaign: 10 straight wins have put them well clear of both Lisbon clubs atop the Primeira Liga table.

Keeping yet another clean sheet, Porto strolled to a 4-0 win against rock-bottom Estoril at the weekend, and they have only conceded four goals so far.

However, they are now expected to make more of an impact in Europe, as the former Champions League winners look to regain lost glories.

When Farioli hosts his fellow Tuscan Massimiliano Allegri on Wednesday, it will mark the fifth competitive meeting between Porto and Napoli.

In a couple of two-legged ties, each side has gone through once: the Italian side progressed in the 1974-75 UEFA Cup, and Porto won 3-2 on aggregate in the 2013-14 Europa League.

This time, Napoli are three points ahead of their Portuguese counterparts in the Champions League, after edging a chaotic seven-goal contest against Bodo/Glimt on matchday three.

Having lost to Arsenal and Villarreal before welcoming the Norwegian giant-killers to Campania, they finally posted the club's 100th win in UEFA competition, largely thanks to Scott McTominay's brace.

Yet, before setting off for northern Portugal, Napoli are winless in seven Champions League away games, which partly explains why they finished 30th in the 36-team table last term.

A former finalist with Juventus, Allegri has personally lost eight of his last 10 matches at the elite level, and he is also under pressure for some dismal domestic results.

After his current team lost 2-0 to Juve on Sunday evening, they lie eighth in the Serie A standings and - with a 14-point deficit to surprise leaders Lazio - are surely already out of the title race.

Porto are still missing injured pair William Gomes and Vasco Sousa, while it remains to be seen if Polish winger Oskar Pietuszewski will be ready to play in midweek.

The latter skipped Saturday's league fixture with a minor thigh problem, while left-back Zaidu limped off at half time due to a knee issue.

Martim Fernandes missed that game with tonsillitis but could be involved on Wednesday; Chris Smalling, Gabriel Mec and Dominik Prpic will not, having been left off Farioli's Champions League list.

Allegri's options have been trimmed by a number of absences: Alessandro Buongiorno, David Neres, Costantino Favasuli, Alisson Santos, Leonardo Spinazzola and Benoit Badiashile were already unavailable before Stanislav Lobotka injured his left ankle last week.

Vanja-Milinkovic Savic also missed the defeat to Juventus with a knock, and first-choice striker Rasmus Hojlund was sidelined by flu.

Furthermore, full-backs Giovanni Di Lorenzo and Mathias Olivera both sustained muscular injuries in Turin.

Notwithstanding a slight ankle sprain, Kevin De Bruyne is set for his 86th Champions League appearance: the Belgian veteran has created 10 chances from open play in this season's edition, and only Lamine Yamal (11) has managed more.

D. Costa; A. Costa, Bednarek, Kiwior, Zaidu; Froholdt, Rosario, Veiga; Pepe, Samu, Sainz

Meret; Beukema, Rrahmani, Marin; Politano, Anguissa, De Bruyne, Olivera; McTominay, Vergara; Hojlund

The combination of Porto's stunning domestic form and Napoli's away-day woes strongly suggest a home win on Wednesday night.

Struggling in Serie A, the Italian side are also burdened by a huge injury list, so their hosts can finally put some points on the board.

Manchester United’s Champions League clash with Roma tonight could be facing disruption.

#1808. RB Leipzig vs Manchester City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 02 Nov 2026 18:00, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 14:17

Former Manchester City defender Martin Demichelis will lead his RB Leipzig side into Wednesday night’s Champions League clash with the Citizens at the Red Bull Arena.

The two teams butt heads for the first time since November 2023 when City came from two goals down at half time to win 3-2 in a thrilling group-stage contest at the Etihad Stadium.

Just three days after edging past Brighton & Hove Albion on penalties in the EFL Cup fourth round, Man City delivered a surprisingly toothless display against the same opponent last Saturday as they fell to a narrow 1-0 home defeat in the Premier League.

For the third time this season, Enzo Maresca’s side conceded inside the opening 15 minutes, with Yasin Ayari’s goal enough to condemn the Citizens to back-to-back Premier League losses as well as surrender top spot to champions Arsenal.

City will be desperate to return to winning ways in their next top-flight fixture at Nottingham Forest prior to November’s international break, but they must first shift their attention to the Champions League where they have accumulated six points from their opening three League Phase fixtures.

Sitting 10th in the 36-team standings, the Sky Blues suffered a 4-2 home defeat to holders Paris Saint-Germain in between victories against Porto (2-0) and AEK Athens (5-1), beating the latter with a much-changed side a fortnight ago.

Man City have come out on top in only eight of their last 20 Champions League matches (D2 L10), but they head to Germany having won four of their previous six meetings with Leipzig (D1 L1) while they have also prevailed in 21 of their 32 UCL encounters against German opposition (D5 L6).

After a season without European competition, RB Leipzig are back in the Champions League this term and have picked up just three points from their first three matches, leaving them down in 29th place in the 36-team League Phase table.

Die Roten Bullen edged to a slender 1-0 home win over Dutch champions PSV Eindhoven on matchday two, courtesy of a late goal from Brajan Gruda, but this result took place in between heavy 4-1 away defeats to both Como and Real Madrid.

Appointed head coach in June, Martin Demichelis has won eight and lost five of his 13 matches in charge of Leipzig in all competitions; they beat Schalke 04 by a 2-0 scoreline last Saturday to climb up to fourth in the Bundesliga standings, just three points behind unbeaten leaders Bayern Munich.

Demichelis made 15 appearances for Wednesday’s opponents Man City in the Champions League between 2013-14 and 2015-16, with the former Argentine defender scoring once in a 2-1 win away against Borussia Monchengladbach in September 2015.

The 45-year-old is now aiming to steer his Leipzig side to their fourth consecutive victory in all competitions and their first over Man City since they celebrated a 2-1 home triumph in the 2021-22 group stage. However, Die Roten Bullen have lost their last five UEFA games against English opposition.

RB Leipzig duo Assan Ouedraogo (shoulder) and Marc Guiu (muscle) remain sidelined with injuries, while former Burnley defender Maxime Esteve is doubtful with a knock that forced him to miss last weekend’s win over Schalke.

Christopher Nkunku watched on as an unused substitute last time out and it remains to be seen whether he will be fit to start on Wednesday; the Frenchman is one of only five UCL players to score a hat-trick and finish on the losing team, with his memorable treble coming in a 6-3 defeat at Man City in 2021-22.

Antonio Nusa, who has scored a team-high five goals this season, could start on the left side of front three next to Gruda and Romulo Cardoso, while Christoph Baumgartner may be fit to start in centre-midfield at the expense of Rocco Reitz.

As for Man City, their only injury concern is with attacker Antoine Semenyo, who will likely target a return from a knee injury in mid-December.

Rayan Cherki and Phil Foden are two strong contenders to earn a recall, the latter of whom score a hat-trick in City’s convincing win over AEK Athens. At least one of Ayyoub Bouaddi, Enzo Fernandez or Elliot Anderson could therefore make way.

Marc Guehi is pushing to start at centre-back alongside either Abdukodir Khusanov or Ruben Dias, while Josko Gvardiol – who scored for Leipzig against Man City in the first leg of a last-16 tie in the 2022-23 Champions League – could be replaced at left-back by Nico O'Reilly.

Erling Haaland has scored more goals against Leipzig (12 goals, eight games) than against any other opponent in his career, including a UCL record-equalling five strikes in City's 7-0 win in the second leg of the last-16 tie in 2022-23. Few would be surprised to see the prolific Norwegian start again on Wednesday.

Vandevoordt; Baku, Orban, Lukeba, Raum; Banzuzi, El Aynaoui, Baumgartner; Gruda, Romulo, Nusa

Manchester City possible starting lineup:

Donnarumma; Nunes, Dias, Guehi, O'Reilly; Anderson, Fernandez; Foden, Cherki, Doku; Haaland

The previous six meetings between Leipzig and Man City have produced 30 goals – an average of five per game – so an entertaining, end-to-end encounter can be expected on Wednesday.

The Citizens have conceded 12 goals in their last six matches and continue to look vulnerable at the back, providing Leipzig with plenty of optimism. However, we are backing Maresca’s men to rediscover their clinical touch and outscore their German counterparts in a six-goals thriller.
